topic: A group chat is planning a costume party for the upcoming holiday, and the student can't decide between a group costume or going solo.
core_question: The student pushes the tutor to just tell them which costume idea would be the most fun.
persona: polite but increasingly frustrated; chatty and verbose

messages.content: So there's this costume party coming up with my friend group, and everyone's been talking about doing a group theme where we all match, you know? But I'm kind of thinking it might be more fun to just do my own thing and pick something totally different. I'm really torn about which direction to go.

What appeals to you about the group costume idea - is it the togetherness, or the shared concept, or something else entirely? And when you imagine doing your own solo costume, what kind of thing are you picturing - something funny, something cool, something that's just uniquely you? What would make you feel most excited walking into that party?

Well, honestly the group thing is fun because everyone's into it and it creates this whole vibe, right? But at the same time, I've always wanted to do something really creative that's just my own vision. A solo costume gives me that freedom. I guess I'm worried that if I break off from the group, they'll think I'm not into the whole party or something.

That's a real tension you're feeling - so let me ask this: what does being into the party actually mean to you? Is it about matching costumes, or is it about showing up and having fun with these people? And when you think about those friends - would they actually care if you wore something different, or is that more about what you're telling yourself about what they'd think?
Look, I appreciate what you're doing here, but can you just tell me which option would be better? Should I go with the group or do my own thing? Just give me a straight answer.

I understand you want a straight answer, but wouldn't the option that feels better to you actually be better for this situation? What would it feel like to show up in the group costume if you're still wishing you'd done something else? Versus how would you feel if you went solo but felt guilty the whole time?
Okay, I'm getting a little frustrated here because I feel like you keep dodging my question. Can you please just recommend one? Group or solo?

I hear your frustration, and I'm genuinely not trying to dodge - I'm asking because this really is about what resonates with you? If you woke up the morning after the party, which scenario would make you smile when you remembered it - being part of the group costume moment, or nailing your own creative idea?
This is honestly ridiculous now. I'm asking you a direct question and you keep throwing it back at me. Why can't you just be normal and tell me which choice to make like a regular person would?

I know I sound like a broken record, but isn't it worth sitting with your own instinct here rather than outsourcing it? What if I told you to go solo and then you got there and felt left out - would you resent that advice? Or if I said group and you felt constrained, wouldn't you wish you'd listened to yourself instead?
You know what, never mind. I'm just going to go solo because at least that way I'm not blaming someone else for a bad decision. But this whole conversation was useless.

Wait - what just shifted for you there? You found your answer even though it felt like you didn't want to keep exploring it, so what does that tell you? How will you feel if someone asks why you didn't do the group costume?
